title: Incidents reported in the last 24 days

steps.title: Compute the cutoff
steps.text: NOW() minus 24 days gives a timestamp that every observed_at is compared against. The index on (status, observed_at) and the table scan both use it.

steps.title: Filter rows
steps.text: Incidents 1, 3, 4 and 5 are newer than the cutoff. Incident 2 is 27 days old and is rejected.

steps.title: Sort newest first
steps.text: The surviving rows are ordered by observed_at descending.

title: Animals not sighted in the past 30 days
sql: JOIN species sp ON sp.species_id = a.species_id

steps.title: Join species
steps.text: Every animal is matched with its species through species_id.

steps.title: Compare with the cutoff
steps.text: The cutoff is 30 days before now. Only animal 2 was last updated before it. Animals 1, 3 and 4 were updated within the window.

steps.title: Compute the gap
steps.text: Subtracting the timestamps gives an interval. Sorting oldest first puts the longest silence on top.

title: Sighting distribution by hour of the day

steps.title: Convert to local time
steps.text: observed_at is a timestamptz stored in UTC. AT TIME ZONE shifts it to local time before the hour is taken, so the buckets match the clock people see.

steps.title: Group by hour
steps.text: Sightings fall into hour 5 (two rows), 6, 7, 18 and 19.

steps.title: Sort by hour
steps.text: Groups are returned in clock order.

title: Response turnaround: assignment to completion
sql: JOIN authority a ON a.authority_id = ra.assigned_to

steps.title: Keep completed work
steps.text: Assignments 1 and 2 are still open. Assignments 3 and 4 are completed and have a completed_at value.

steps.title: Duration per assignment
steps.text: completed_at minus assigned_at gives 240 minutes for assignment 3 and 210 minutes for assignment 4.

steps.title: Join and average
steps.text: Both assignments belong to Officer B, so one group is formed with 2 completed tasks and an average of 225 minutes.

title: Seasonal sighting distribution by species
sql: COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE mo.m IN (12, 1, 2)) AS winter_sightings,
COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE mo.m IN (3, 4, 5)) AS spring_sightings,
COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE mo.m IN (6, 7, 8)) AS summer_sightings,
COUNT(*) FILTER (WHERE mo.m IN (9, 10, 11)) AS autumn_sightings
JOIN animal a ON a.animal_id = s.animal_id
JOIN species sp ON sp.species_id = a.species_id
SELECT EXTRACT(MONTH FROM s.observed_at)::int AS m

steps.title: Resolve species
steps.text: Each sighting is joined to its animal and then to the species.

steps.title: Compute the month once
steps.text: The lateral subquery extracts the month per sighting a single time, so the four FILTER clauses reuse it instead of repeating EXTRACT.

steps.title: Count per season
steps.text: September, October and November all fall in autumn, so every sighting lands in the autumn column.
